findings.what: DMM v3 JSON intent format and ops usable for this mod
findings.where: DMM.exe dmm-parser\src\intents\apply.rs + src\iteminfo\field_json_v3.rs strings; existing mods in Desktop\DMM 3.5.0\mods
findings.evidence: Record shape: {file:'characterinfo.pabgb', intents:[{entry:'<string_key>', key:<u32>, field:'<path>', op, new|value, label, match/where, optional}]}. Generic ops: set, array_append, list_union, clone_record (source_key/new_key), new_record (new_key + template; '_blob_fallback'/'_blob_b64' for raw records), delete_record. iteminfo-path list ops: list_set, list_remove (where with operators, optional:true), list_append, list_extend, list_merge (merge_key). Load-order keys: priority, before, after, conflicts_with, conflict_override. A table can be named as .pabgb or .staticinfobody. Example: Combat Evolved.json uses set on 'entries[0].etl_hashes' with a full list; Equip All Armor.json uses match on equip_type_info. Note: DMM 2.x changelog 'Known' said interaction overrides plus the mercenary and interaction tables were 'still being decoded' and edits to them were skipped. 3.5.0 has the typed structs but keeps raw tails (InteractionTail.Raw._b64, CharacterInfo _tail_b64).

dead_ends: I did not find the InteractionType enum names as a string list in the exe: the enum is read as a byte, and the AICondition_CanInteractionType vtable methods reference no strings. The client-side send path for TrocTr*Req packets is not mapped: the Req vtables are only referenced by static prototype initialisers (227E50/227FE0/228080, edx=0x65), so I don't know how the client serialises and sends one. The cheat-hire handler 2A302D0 only deserialises a 4-byte payload; where it executes is not found. There is no developer cheat-command string table (only 'DevCheat', 'TestCheat', 'SaveByCheat'). Tracing callers of sql->createMercenary (2779860) gave only false 'jmp' hits in obfuscated bytes (4CFxxxx-4D9xxxx). The second accompany caller chain 2BC96C0 -> 2BCA3D0/2BCA9C0 -> 28F82A0/2BC7670/2BC9200 has no strings or vtables, so it stays unnamed. F573B0 (picks the Wait/Follow label) belongs to UIGamePlayControlCommonCharacterDescription, not to the command sender. Greymane membership by _factionInfo (Faction_Graymane key 1000000 = 0x0F4240) cannot be read by byte scan: 7038 character records contain 0x0F4240 because other tables also start their keys at 1000000. It needs a proper characterinfo schema parse (the DMM schema). I did not parse the full CharacterInfo records, so the current _isHirable, _mercenaryInfo and _aiScriptPathHash values of Yahn/Nairah and the others are unknown. Scratch artifacts: scratchpad\ (struct_fields.json = field lists of 537 structs from the exe; charnames.json = 7250 CharacterKey->name; interaction_names.json = 437 InteractionKey->name; leaidx.npz rip-relative ref index; helpers sref.py, vt.py, qref.py, enumtab.py, enumdump.py, fields.py). The tables/ subfolder is shared with other agents. Nothing was written to the game or DMM folders.

findings.what: Reflection data format of .paseqc (gameplay data of a sequence), fully decoded by a scratch tool
findings.where: scratchpad\py\refl.py (decoder), schema.py, summ.py (per-file outline), batch.py, follow.py, aistats.py
findings.evidence: The schema header is the same as in .palevel/.prefab. Data layout: 16-byte header (u32 0, u32 1, u32 file size, u32 0). Root: u64 id, u32 self, u32 total, u16 bitmapLen, bitmap, u32 0, then fields. Every other object: u16 bitmapLen, bitmap (one presence bit per declared field), u16 class index, u8 0, u64 id, u32 self-offset (points just past itself), u32 0, the field values, then a trailing u32 payload size. Lists (kinds 3/7/10) are always present: u8 1 means empty, otherwise u8 0, u32 count, then the items (kind 7 lists have a 13-byte list header before their objects). Kind 5 pointers: u8 0 = null, 1 = an object follows. Strings are u32 length + bytes. 3065 of 3066 .paseqc files decode exactly to end of file; cd_seq_quest_maze_forest_kusunsla_5900 fails on a kind-6 field. .paseq (editor timeline) starts with an indexed string table and was not decoded. .pastage is a separately compiled stage chart: template name, sections, condition strings and opcodes with argument keys.
findings.relevance: Makes cloning and editing sequences possible in principle; an encoder is straightforward from this layout. The open risk is .pastage: tags are also compiled there (set_playerAlly -> 0x11554), so editing .paseqc tags alone may not change behaviour. The template sources (quest/stagechart_common2, funcnpc/funcnpc_interaction) are not in the archives.

findings.what: Party and AI events only last for their timeline time range; there is no persistent follower state in the sequencer itself
findings.where: _timelineList and _timelineEventList in decoded .paseqc files
findings.evidence: PLAY sections are short time ranges (for example PLAY_0 0..1799) whose tags wait on conditions. Cutscene and AI sections are longer (beforescout_0080 PLAY_2 82440..320039, bloodthrone SCENE_2 5400..884459). Party events span exactly their section, and the stage ends with Timeline.branch(Terminate). Stages also have world boundaries and terminate_* rules. The only persistent hand-off is set_accompanyMercenary at the end of bloodthrone_0100 (Oongka/Damian), which goes to the mercenary/accompany system.
findings.relevance: For world-wide following, a stage would have to stay running (boundary and region unloading are a risk). The accompany-mercenary system is persistent, so it is a better fit than a sequencer Party for 'follow me around the world'.

Console command names are not stored as plain text in the exe ('/automatedteststart' appears only in profiling sequences), and no hire or party cheat command name was found.

Raw u32 searches for interaction keys across tables give many false hits because key ranges overlap. The u32 lists inside mercenaryinfo records are an ambiguous key type (partly formation keys).

The stage chart templates (quest/stagechart_common2, funcnpc/funcnpc_interaction, weatherring) exist only in compiled form inside each .pastage; the .pastage function bytecode was only partly decoded.

dead_ends: No table is literally named companion, follower or party; mercenaryinfo and mercenarygroupinfo are that system. uitalktreeinfo is only the social-conversation minigame. Npc_Employ ('Recruit'), Npc_Order_Follow_Defensive and Npc_Order_Disband are in no characterinfo interaction list, and no table, .pastage or .paseq references them by name. Raw u32 searches give many false hits because every table numbers its keys from 0xf4240 up (for example 0xf4292 is also aidialog type 'Management_Waiting'). Only field-aware parsing is reliable. Interaction names, their hashlittle values and their key immediates do not appear in CrimsonDesert.exe, so how an interaction is bound to its code is not visible statically; the distinct per-interaction hashes in the interaction tail are a lead. hashlittle(lower,810718) names the ally groups ('player', 'npc') but not the appearance/prefab hashes in characterinfo, and ally group 0x9407ece0 stays unnamed. The 40-byte flag run after the override blocks could not be named: flag index 38 (Naira at +0x18c) is 0 on every hireable human comrade and 1 on about 7087 of 7189 other records, so it may be hire-related (unverified). The mercenary override block is zero (valid=0) even on working hired comrades, so it is not what lets them fight. Nothing in vanilla hires the Naira/Yann/Witch companion records: no Mercenary(...) drop set and no condition mentions them. Not done, because the rules forbid it: running the game, attaching to it, or testing the DMM JSON in practice. DMM's exact names for the mercenary-type and hire-message fields (probably f37/f38) are unconfirmed.
